newsitem.title: USA: U.S. February budget deficit $44.01 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. February budget deficit $44.01 bln.

text.p: The government posted a budget deficit of $44.01 billion in February, the Treasury Department said on Friday, down slightly from the $44.35 billion deficit posted in February 1996.
The February deficit followed a $13.36 billion surplus in January.
Total outlays in February were $134.30 billion, down from $137.35 billion in January but up from $133.78 billion in February 1996.
Revenues from taxes, fees and other sources fell to $90.29 billion in February from $150.72 billion in January. In February 1996, the government took in $89.43 billion of revenues.
During the first five months of fiscal 1997, which began on Oct 1, the cumulative budget deficit was $89.96 billion up from $80.64 billion in the comparable first five months of fiscal 1996.

The budget is typically in surplus in January because there is a bulge in tax payments at the start of the calendar year as individuals who make quarterly estimated payments send them in and corporations send in year-end payments.

During February, receipts from individual tax payments dropped back to $37.4 billion from $87.24 billion in January. Corporate tax payments fell to $2.24 billion in February from $4.81 billion a month earlier.
The Clinton administration has forecast a deficit for all of fiscal 1997 of $125.59 billion, up from a deficit of $106.99 billion in fiscal 1996.
